newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. proposes tax cut,boost in school funds.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. proposes tax cut,boost in school funds.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson on Tuesday proposed a 10 percent cut in business and corporation taxes, a boost in school funding and an overhaul of the state's welfare system.
In his State of the State address, Wilson, a Republican, said the 10 percent tax cut would be phased in over two years and was designed create jobs and boost the economy.
"We must continue to slash the hidden tax of overregulation and overreaching that drives investors out of the state," Wilson said in the address.
Wilson called for changes to the legal system that "has made the lawyer's briefcase a weapon of terror that threatens to undermine California's economy."

Wilson proposed as part of his fiscal plan a nearly $1.3 billion class size reduction programme and a $2 billion bond issue for school construction. Wilson also asked the Legislature to invest hundreds of millions of dollars for computers in high schools throughout the state.
The governor also called for "meaningful" reform to the state's endangered species act.
Wilson said student fees would not be increased at the state's universities for the third year in a row.
Wilson said he would release a more detailed plan to "end welfare" when he submits his budget.
Wilson was scheduled to present his fiscal year 1997-1998 budget proposal on Thursday.
Spokesman Sean Walsh said the budget was not expected to make provisions for flood recovery.
